reasoning_content: The `pkill -f` command is killing its own shell because the shell's command line (the bash -c containing the pkill pattern) matches the pattern. That's why it exits with 143. Let me use a more targeted kill.

action.command:
cd /workspace && nohup pnpm exec tsx /tmp/launch-app2.mjs > /tmp/launch5.log 2>&1 & sleep 4; cat /tmp/launch5.log
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 http://localhost:3000/health/live 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "live up after ~$((i*5))s"; break; }
  sleep 5
done
echo "=== /auth/me (no session, expect 401) ==="
curl -s -o /tmp/me.txt -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/auth/me; head -c 200 /tmp/me.txt; echo
